summary:
UNSAFE TO PLAY UNTIL THE NEXT ENGINEER IS DONE (server and client were left untouched; `git diff 546c1e1 -- packages/server packages/client scripts tests` is empty):
1. A pilot who touches down gently on a landable body is stuck. Shared code now turns the touch into FlightMode.Landed, the server stops stepping that ship (packages/server/src/sim.ts:267) and the client stops sending input (packages/client/src/game/Game.ts:91 isFlying). The way out today is to reload the page: logout saves the state, isUsableState (world.ts:782) rejects mode Landed, and the pilot comes back docked at home. I read that path in the code; I did not run it.
2. Hard ground impacts do no damage (nobody reads StepEnv.impact), and flying into a landable body no longer destroys the ship: the exclusion radius is gone there and the terrain, which the client does not draw yet, pushes the ship out instead.
3. Cruise that ends at a ceiling emits no cruise-off event or notice (nobody reads StepEnv.cruiseDrop).
4. Within 60 to 300 km of a landable body ships are now in the rotating surface frame, and the client still draws ship, camera, contacts, effects and the velocity marker as if those axes were system axes.
5. Local delivery missions can name a ground base, and nobody can dock at one yet. Bases are also invisible on clients (they carry no model key, see below).
Stations, gas giants, stars, black holes and everything far from landable ground behave as before; the 412 existing tests pass with six expectations changed where the specification changes behaviour.

What is now true in packages/shared: one body-rotation helper that matches Bodies.ts; the terrain (the earlier engineer's design kept, tested, one bound fixed, and made free of garbage); surface anchors 500 + bodyId with anchorFrame, exact reanchor/absolutePosition/absoluteVelocity/absoluteRotation between any two frames; automatic frame crossing in simulateShip; Coriolis and centrifugal terms with flight assist cancelling them; ground contact, landing, bounce with reported impact, the Landed mode and lift-off; cruise limits, ceiling drop and the 'ground' block near landable bodies; ground bases as sites with pads, placement and mass lock; a generator that appends bases from its own random stream without changing any existing system (checked against hashes captured from 546c1e1); protocol version 4, FlightMode.Landed = 5, EntityFlag.Landed = 128; a section in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md.

Two deliberate deviations from the specification, both forced by the browser run:
- `base_ground` is NOT in STRUCTURES and bases carry no `model`. The client preloads the model of every STRUCTURES entry at start (packages/client/src/render/local/objects/index.ts:64) and of every site that names one (structures.ts:297); the missing file is a 404 console error on every page, which fails scripts/e2e.mjs (seen in run 2). The shape is exported as GROUND_BASE_STRUCTURE in shared/structures.ts.
- Bases are generated only in inhabited systems (those with a faction, that is with a station or outpost). Otherwise a summary would count a base-only system as having a station and scripts/e2e.mjs:393/477 would pick it and fail; it also keeps "faction defined iff somewhere to dock" true.

Final state: tsc x3 clean, 488 tests pass (412 existing + 76 new), client builds, scripts/e2e.mjs ended "e2e ok" on the final tree (third browser run; the first two are explained under verification). Nothing about landing has been exercised through the server or a browser.

behaviour:
BODY ROTATION. bodyRotation(body, t) = tilt about system +X by `tilt`, applied after a spin about the body's +Y axis by t / rotPeriod turns (negative period spins the other way; only the fraction of a turn is used). bodyAngularVelocity = bodySpinAxis * 2 pi / rotPeriod. It equals the inverse of what Bodies.ts builds with three.js to 9e-16 (checked numerically in a scratch script for 6 tilts x 3 periods x 4 times; the two differ only at tilt exactly pi, where three picks another axis).

FRAMES. Anchor ids: 0..499 bodies, 500 + bodyId surface frame, >= 1000 sites. The generator throws if a system has 500 bodies or more. In a surface frame pos, vel and rot are in body-fixed rotating axes, origin at the body centre. anchorState works for every id (surface anchor = body state; ground site = pad position with omega x r in the velocity). A surface anchor is valid only for a landable body. reanchor converts position, velocity (taking off omega x r of the old frame, adding that of the new) and orientation; between a body frame and its own surface frame nothing of orbital size is added, so it is exact to 1e-8 m.

WHERE THE SURFACE FRAME APPLIES. surfaceFrameAltitude = clamp(0.1 * radius, 60 km, 300 km) above the mean radius. In normal flight simulateShip moves a ship into the surface frame when its centre distance falls below radius + that height, from whatever anchor it had (body, other body, orbital site), and back into the non-rotating frame of the same body above radius + 1.3 times that height. pickNormalAnchor returns the surface anchor below the lower height before it looks at sites, so a freshly placed ship keeps its frame on its first tick; disengageCruise with a named site obeys the same rule. Cruise uses body anchors only. A ground site is never a flight anchor.

PHYSICS THERE. buildStepEnv gives the sources in frame axes, omega = [0, spin rate, 0] and the ground. Normal flight integrates gravity (tidal form, as before) plus -2 omega x v - omega x (omega x r). Flight assist subtracts the same sum, so a ship with no input holds still over the ground; with assist off it follows the same path as in the non-rotating frame (within 2 m after 120 s at up to 900 m/s on a body turning once in 4 h).

GROUND CONTACT (stepShip, normal flight, surface frame). Skipped above radius + terrainMax + belly. Otherwise one full-detail terrain sample under the ship; contact when |pos| < radius + terrain + belly. On contact the origin is set back to that height along the local vertical and the ground normal is measured over max(2 * hull radius, 10 m). sink = speed into the ground along the normal, side = speed along it. Landing when sink <= 6 m/s and side <= 8 m/s and slope <= 20 degrees and the ship's up axis is within 30 degrees of the normal: mode Landed, velocity, spin and pending aim zero, up along the normal, heading kept. Otherwise a collision: normal speed becomes 0.25 of the incoming speed outward, tangential speed is multiplied by 0.9 (per tick of contact), and env.impact = sqrt(max(0, sink - 6)^2 + max(0, side - 8)^2); a gentle touch on too steep ground or with the ship tilted reports 0. env.impact is 0 on every other tick in a surface frame and undefined elsewhere.

LANDED. Position and orientation do not change by a bit; energy, shield, heat, boost timers and charge run as in flight with the star's heat influx; signature = 0.25 * (idle term + heat term) * radius / 12, times 0.08 when silent. Lift-off when thrust up > 0.2, or when the boost button is held and a boost is available (cooldown over, 30 energy): the ship gets 3 m/s along its up axis and the same tick continues as normal flight. No other input does anything. With flight assist the ship then hovers about a metre up; without it and without thrust it hops and lands again. simulateShip gives a Landed ship the full environment (for heat and for hazardsAt) and never re-anchors or samples terrain for it.

CRUISE NEAR LANDABLE BODIES. ceiling = radius + terrainMax + 2,000 m. cruiseSpeedLimit = min(old limit over the other bodies, clamped to at least 30 km/s; max(250 m/s, 0.28/s * height above the nearest ceiling)). The floor used for zero throttle and the clamp is min(30 km/s, limit). Below the ceiling simulateShip ends cruise: surface frame, mode Normal, 100 m/s along the nose over the ground, cruiseSpeed 0, env.cruiseDrop = true on that tick, no impact. canEngageCruise answers 'ground' below a ceiling (order: mode, charging, fuel, masslock, ground). engageCruise starts at cruiseSpeedFloor (e.g. 840 m/s 3 km above the ceiling). hazardsAt never reports insideBody for a landable body. Everything else about cruise, and all of it at other bodies, is unchanged.

GROUND BASES. Site kind 'base', ground = { body, pos } with |pos| = radius + natural terrain height at that direction, orbit = { parent: body, rest 0 }, frameRadius 0, radius 250, no model. The terrain of the body gets a pad there: flat within 400 m at that height, blending over a further 400 m. groundSitePose gives the pose in the surface frame and in system axes (up = pad normal, nose north). isMassLocked includes bases (4 km). placeAtSite(ground site, d) puts the ship in the surface frame d metres from the pad centre, above it and up to min(150 m, d/2) to one side, at rest over the ground, level, on a random heading; orbital sites as before. A docked ship keeps the site id as anchor; absolutePosition handles that.

GENERATOR. buildBases runs after everything else from rngFor(seed, serverId, index, 'bases'). Only systems with a faction get bases. Hosts: landable bodies with G m / r^2 <= 6. The capital gets one if it has a host; other systems with 40 % chance; with a base, 25 % chance of a second on another body. Spot: the most level of 24 random directions, by max(relief over 400 m / 400, relief over 800 m / 800). Services market, refuel, repair, missions, plus outfit in 30 %; economy mining (60 %) or outpost; faction = the system's; name from baseName. Measured over 640 systems: 177 bases in 149 systems; 19 of 20 capitals had a host and all 19 have a base; 162 uninhabited systems with a host get none; 40 bases stand under a station. summarize(): stations = def.stations + bases, tag 'base' (at most 12 tags).

TERRAIN (the earlier engineer's design, kept). Lattice gradient noise with an integer hash on the 3D point direction * radius: 5 continent octaves from 0.9 radii, ridged mountains (6 octaves from 30 to 120 km) under a mask in the highlands (none on ice), 12 roughness octaves from 20 km to 10 m, craters in size classes with lattice cells from 32 m doubling up to 0.2 radii (diameters about 4 m to 0.1 radii; bowl, rim, ejecta, flat floor above 12 km; density 0.9 rocky, 0.45 desert, 0.2 ice), long ridges on ice, dunes on desert; soft compression to guaranteed bounds; pads. Relief bounds: -6.4 to +7.9 km on a 1,737 km rocky moon, -2.9 to +1.1 km on an 800 km ice moon. Tone: dark plains against bright highlands, bright fresh craters with rays, dark ridges on ice, pale dunes. Only + - * /, sqrt, floor, abs, min, max, imul and 32-bit integer operations. Fractional arguments and results of the hot functions go through one module-level Float64Array, so sampling produces no garbage.
